content: Don Pepin Garcia is a premium cigar brand that is entirely hand-made and owned by El Rey de los Habanos, Inc. The brand was established by José Pepín García and is produced in two locations: the El Rey de los Habanos factory in Little Havana, Miami, Florida, and the Tabacalera Cubana factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. The brand offers three distinct ranges of cigars, each varying in strength. All cigars are crafted using Nicaraguan tobaccos in different combinations. The boxes are stamped with a date code to indicate their production time. Don Pepin Garcia Blue Label The Blue Label was the first range introduced by the brand, followed by the Serie JJ. It includes six vitolas and one limited release, the Lancero. These cigars are full-bodied and are not recommended for novice smokers. The wrapper is an oily Nicaraguan Corojo leaf, described as having a cinnamon-like color. The cigars are packaged in cedar boxes containing 25 cigars, which were initially uncellophaned but began to be cellophaned in the summer of 2007. The band is blue with gold lettering, featuring Don Pepin Garcia in gold on a blue field surrounded by a red and gold border. Don Pepín's signature appears below the name. The band also includes overlapping U.S. and Cuban flags within roundels. Ratings and Awards The Invictos received a rating of 88 in the August 2006 issue of Cigar Aficionado magazine. The Magnate was rated 89 in the February 2007 issue of Cigar Aficionado magazine. Don Pepin Garcia Black Edition (Cuban Classic/Black Label) The Black Edition is the newest range in the brand and was introduced for national distribution in the U.S. in late 2006. These cigars are manufactured at the Tabacalera Cubana factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. They are uncellophaned and packaged in cedar cabinets of 20 cigars. The cigars are wrapped with a colored ribbon and a label that reads Don Pepin Garcia along with a facsimile of his signature. The band design is similar to the Blue Label but features a black background. A second band is present, which is a straight band with gold borders on a black background, displaying the words Cuban Classic in gold. The sides of the box are stamped with 20 / Don Pepín (in script) / ♦ BLACK EDITION ♦ / frontmark. The month and year of manufacture are stamped on the bottom of the box. Ratings and Awards The entire range was reviewed in a vertical tasting report in the May 22, 2007, issue of Cigar Insider. The 1979 received the highest rating of 92, while the 1973 received the lowest rating of 85. The 1952 was rated 88, and the 1950, 1970, and 1977 each received a rating of 89. Don Pepin Garcia Serie JJ (White Label) The Serie JJ range was developed by Don Pepín and his son, Jaime García. These cigars are mediumto full-bodied and feature a light-brown Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper. They are packaged in plain boxes of 24 cigars, except for the Salomon vitola, which comes in boxes of five. The band design is similar to the Blue Label but is white with a red border. A second straight band is also present, white in color, with Serie JJ printed on it. The Salomons are exclusively rolled by Don Pepín himself. Notes The Serie JJ was mentioned in the February 2007 issue of Cigar Aficionado (p. 172).
